_readme: STAGING DNA — the small set of artifact TYPES, each defined as the full environment it needs: staging (footing that grows the grid) + support (the station prop it stands on/against) + dressing (light, caption, cordon that make it read). Promoted from the Element Catalog (posture_to_station.json): that file names the correspondence, THIS file is the buildable template. Keyed by posture id (what tools/classify_postures.py assigns). Rendered by DressingRoomBuilder staged mode. Offsets are [rows_south, cols_east, y_metres] relative to the ANCHOR cell, rotated with the room. cfg values may substitute {height_m} (raised-region top), {raised_w}/{raised_d} (its extent in cells).
_text_model: TWO text slots per artifact, filled from the registry automatically in the SUPPORT's cfg: {artifact} = the TITLE (short name) → the support's own SCREEN HEADER (info_header / screen_header); {info_lines} = the SIMULATION INFO (registry description wrapped to short lines) → the support's own INTEGRATED SCREEN (info_lines / screen_lines). ONE BODY principle: text is set INTO the prop (a lit console readout that is part of the plinth / bench / wall), never a floating plate or a separate panel beside it. No lamps — the light is integrated (plinth cap glow). Props without a screen surface yet (stage/skydome/barrier) carry no text until their own console lands.
_edge_cases: Deferred, deliberately: SUPER-LARGE artifacts (base > ~8m — koch_curve, shader galleries) need a 'monument' type where the environment recedes entirely; KINETIC artifacts that sweep a volume need clearance the AABB alone can't predict; MULTI-artifact bays are curation_station's job, not a single-room template.

specimen.essence: A small thing held up to the eye. The museum pose: one object on ONE BODY — a column that is its own mount, its own lit screen (title + info), its own light, wired together. Nothing floats beside it.

support.note: ONE BODY: the TITLE is the screen header, the INFO is the lit screen set into the front face, the LIGHT is the cap glow, and a lit conduit wires cap→screen. No lamp, no floating plate. Minimal finish (grime/dust/three_bar off).

instrument.essence: A thing you operate with your hands. Worktop height, light on the controls, room to stand square in front of it.

support.note: ONE BODY: the info reads on the bench's own back-standing console (built in, on a strut) — no lamp, no floating plate

dressing.why: zone edge - the lit line where the instrument's station ENDS (R-019 station_on_aisle)

performer.essence: A body that commands a stage. Raised so the whole form reads at distance; a lip that says LOOK, don't touch.

support.note: station_stage clamps to 0.35 — a dais is LOW by identity; top_m reseats the artifact on the real deck, not the blockout height

terrain.essence: The artifact IS the ground. Nothing under it, nothing on it — a flush pad, an edge that marks where it begins, and sightlines from above.

dressing.why: threshold strip where the walkway meets the work

apparition.essence: A hovering field with no base. Air gap instead of a plinth; a void behind it so the edgeless thing has nothing to be measured against.
apparition.support_gap: no suspension prop exists yet (gantry-hoist / ceiling point) — the lift is bare artifact_offset

dressing.why: the shadow line - the hover meets the floor by LIGHT, not contact (R-019 pole_on_floor's cousin)

well.essence: A thing you look down into. The rim does the staging: raise the viewer, sink the subject, guard the edge.

dressing.why: guard the approach edge, standing on the rim

tableau.essence: A flat thing read frontally. A face to hang on, light raking the surface, a caption at reading height.

support.note: ONE BODY: the info reads on the wall's built-in screen slot — no lamp, no floating plate

dressing.why: skirting - the wall's ending read at the floor (R-018 wall_on_floor)

monument.essence: Too big to be an object. A super-large or very-long artifact (an 86 m portal corridor, a field, a tower) shown at TRUE SCALE — the environment recedes: no plinth, no props, no lamp. Just the thing, a frame marking its REAL extent, and a human-scale post. It is a SPACE, reviewed as one.

dressing.why: the ground line - where the monument's ground ends before it stops existing (R-019)

monument.note: Auto-assigned by classify_postures when the size oracle's max_dimension_m > ~12 m (and it isn't flat). Rendered like the floor type (flush at y=0, no props/pillar) PLUS the builder draws an ACCENT footprint frame at the artifact's true grid_cells extent (from artifact_sizes.json) + a 1.8 m scale post. These belong in the spine / generative-corridor map pipeline — walked, not staged as an object.

_meets: R-019 DNA PUSH: every type declares HOW IT MEETS. The reveal (cap_inset) is explicit data, not a silent prop default; types with no articulated meet get one: the instrument's zone edge, the apparition's shadow line (it meets the floor by LIGHT, not contact), the tableau's skirting, the monument's ground line. The joint is the generator of form — see station_modules.json junctions + doc/book/RULINGS.md R-018/R-019.
